action: AI app operators: confirm a valid legal basis, such as explicit consent, before training models on sensitive user data, and tell users how their data is used.
date_note: GBA page last updated 17 November 2026; decision 320/2026 is dated 16 November 2026.
exec: Regulators are enforcing data protection rules on how AI products use sensitive user conversations.
plain: Belgium's privacy regulator reprimanded a chatbot app, which it does not name, for training its AI on sensitive user conversations without a valid legal basis.
summary: Belgium's data protection authority (GBA) reprimanded an unnamed chatbot app after a complaint that it processed personal data without a valid legal basis to train chatbots. The GBA found no valid legal basis for training on sensitive conversation data and too little transparency; it found legitimate interest valid for normal data. The company has four months to comply or faces a penalty payment of 1,000 euros per day.
title: Belgian DPA reprimands chatbot app over training on sensitive conversation data

validation.note: GBA's own page and Security.nl both state the decision.
